title: Sudden awakening
hookLine: Huineng's southern school taught that awakening is sudden; the northern school stressed the gradual

cards: Anyone who learned to ride a bike can tell it two ways. One way: it took weeks. Scraped knees, a hand on the back of the seat, more wobbly starts than anyone counted.
The other way: it happened in an instant. One afternoon the hand let go, and suddenly you were riding. Both stories are true, told from different ends.
Chan Buddhism in China told its own version of this argument, about awakening, and attached it to two teachers already met at the wall with their verses.

teach.b: The Platform Sutra speaks of a southern teaching and a northern one: Huineng in the south, Shenxiu in the north. It links the south with sudden awakening and the north with the gradual.
The verses show the two emphases. Shenxiu's said: wipe the mirror again and again, let no dust settle. That's patient, steady practice, a little cleaner each day.
Huineng's answered: from the beginning there is nothing for dust to land on. That's seeing, all at once, what was already so. Then the surprise: the sutra doesn't let the argument end there.
In paraphrase, Huineng says the teaching itself is neither sudden nor gradual. People are quicker or slower, and that is where the difference lies. The way is one.
The pace belongs to the walker. Read like that, sudden and gradual aren't rival camps. They're the bike story told from both ends: the long wobbling, and the instant it clicks.
And this week has had both in it. The Xinxin Ming: the great way is not hard, without picking and choosing. A hair's breadth, and heaven and earth apart.
Don't seek the true, just stop holding opinions.
Not two. A woodcutter who heard a sutra through a doorway. No-thought, not stuck.
Any one of those can land in an instant. Any one of them can also take years of mornings to live.

how: Zen and Chan schools discuss sudden and gradual awakening in talks and study, and some teachers present them as two sides of practice rather than rival paths.

o: awakening with no practice ever needed
a flash of insight that fades by morning
seeing at once what was already so

games.q: in Huineng's own sutra, the question comes up: is the way sudden or gradual? what does the text answer?
o: sudden, and the gradual is wrong
the teaching is neither; people are quicker or slower

games.why: even in the sutra of the 'sudden' school, Huineng says the teaching has no sudden or gradual. the difference is in people.

practice: Notice that each breath arrives whole, all at once, the moment it's here, and that the sitting settles slowly, a little at a time; let both be true.

Then bring to mind someone whose pace differs from yours, who goes slowly where you rush or leaps where you plod. Hold them in mind for a few breaths with some respect, as another walker on the same road.

wordCard.voice: Sudden awakening. The teaching the Platform Sutra links with Huineng's southern school, beside the north's gradual way, and the sutra's own reminder that the teaching itself has no speeds. Today's word.

orig.note: Chinese (dunwu): 'sudden awakening', the teaching the Platform Sutra links with the south.

carryVoice: Your line: sudden and gradual. Quick or slow, it's one road. That's a week of both.
